audit_2026_10_18: Source audit (live Socrata API, 2026-10-18): dataset 7fq7-8j7r 'EBR Building Permits' on data.brla.gov, attribution 'Permits and Inspections' (the City-Parish's Department of Permits and Inspections), license Public Domain (views-API metadata), dataset description 'All construction and occupancy permits issued in East Baton Rouge Parish'. 144,453 rows all-time; issueddate range 2011-10-10 to 2026-10-16; rowsUpdatedAt 2026-10-18T11:23:26Z (refreshed the morning of the pull). OPERATIONAL NOTE: the portal's aggregate reads lagged the data during the audit — an early window count(*) read 7,546 while two full paged pulls agreed on 8,500 rows row-for-row (identical row sets) and a later count(*) agreed at 8,500 (the mid-reload lag pattern San Francisco showed in session 3). Every build measurement below is from full pulls verified twice; gate 4's pre-pull count baseline protects future runs the same way. IDENTITY (trailing-12-month window, issueddate >= 2025-10-17): 8,500 rows = 8,482 distinct permits; permitid and permitnumber are strictly 1:1 (8,482 pairs; no id maps to two numbers, no number to two ids). The grain is one row per ADDRESS a permit covers (the San Francisco pattern): 7 permits fan out (5 with 2 rows, 1 with 4, 1 with 11 — the 11-row permit is one security-camera permit covering 11 locations), and 2 rows are verbatim duplicates inside those groups; the surplus is exactly 18 = 8,500 - 8,482. Sibling rows disagree on NONE of issueddate, creationdate, permittype, designation, projectdescription, projectvalue, permitfee, squarefootage, or parishname (measured on the full window, re-asserted by the pipeline's collapse on the production pull); they vary only on streetaddress, city1, zip, and — in 2 permits — contractorname. All-time the same grain holds (a 2023 multi-site permit fans out to 52 address rows under one permitid). COVERAGE: parishname is 'East Baton Rouge' on 100% of window rows and the dataset describes itself as all construction and occupancy permits issued in the parish; the issuer is the consolidated City-Parish government. city1 is a free-text mailing-city field (Baton Rouge in many spellings, plus Zachary, Baker, Greenwell Springs, Pride, Slaughter, Jackson, Clinton) — normalized for display only, never used to scope coverage. PRIVACY: the dataset publishes ownername and applicantname (person names) and contractoraddress; all three are excluded from the pull's column list entirely and never enter our records. The only name carried is contractorname, the permit's published contractor of record (a real value on 4,849 of 8,482 window permits; 'N/A' on the rest, carried as NULL). DESIGNATION (category): Residential 5,088 permits / Commercial 2,290 / none stated 1,104. STATUS: the dataset publishes no status field at all; it is an issued-permits register (every row carries an issueddate; zero null issueddates all-time), so records carry status 'issued' with no source status text. VALUATION (projectvalue, a number column, published on 100% of window permits, 0 nulls): permit level — 3,016 at $0 (35.6%; concentrated in occupancy permits, 95-98% of which state no value because they authorize a use rather than construction; the construction families state real values at 93-100%), 74 at $1 (0.9%), 5,392 above $1; total $955,314,596.87; median positive value $14,826. STAMP SCAN: no value above $5M repeats at a different address anywhere in the window (the Seattle disease is absent); the most-repeated large values are round applicant budgets ($1,500,000 x7, $1,200,000 x4 — the Boston signature of round declared estimates). Two disclosed as-reported shapes: (a) one 224-unit multifamily project at 3 Smart Way states the same $44,688,000 project value on each of its three separate building permits (same address, same description, same contractor — the Boston restatement shape; if the figure is whole-project on all three, the overstatement is bounded at $89,376,000, 9.4% of the window total); (b) the largest permit ($180,000,000, 18.8% of the total) is a land-clearing permit for a private rail yard at 14225 Scenic Hwy carrying its whole project's stated value — the Chicago shape; its description prints alongside on the pages. The naive row-level sum ($956,174,580.87) overstates the permit-level total by only 0.09% because multi-address fan-out is rare in this window. September 2026 cross-check targets (permit grain, independently computed from a source-side pull grouped by permitid): 722 permits / $191,526,496.58 (API row count for September: 732). October 2026 to date at audit: 372 permits; freshest issueddate 2026-10-16.
coverage_note: Permits issued by the East Baton Rouge City-Parish Department of Permits and Inspections; the dataset describes itself as all construction and occupancy permits issued in East Baton Rouge Parish. The feed counts each permit once even when it covers several addresses (see dedupe_rule).

dedupe_rule.definition: A 'permit' for East Baton Rouge Parish = one permitid issued by the City-Parish Department of Permits and Inspections (permitid and permitnumber are the same permit's two identifiers, strictly 1:1). The feed's grain is one row per ADDRESS a permit covers: a permit covering 11 camera locations appears as 11 rows sharing one permitid, one issue date, one type, and one stated project value, differing in street address. The pipeline collapses each permit's rows into one record (registry collapse_events) before normalization; the record is represented by the permit's first row in pull order (issue date, permit id, street address, contractor name), because the source publishes no primary-address flag.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (issueddate >= 2025-10-17), measured 2026-10-18 on full pulls verified twice row-for-row: 8,500 rows vs 8,482 distinct permitid (= 8,482 distinct permitnumber, strictly 1:1). 7 permits fan out to multiple rows (5 x 2, 1 x 4, 1 x 11) and 2 rows are verbatim duplicates inside those groups; surplus 18 = 8,500 - 8,482. Across all multi-row permits the rows disagree on NONE of issueddate, creationdate, permittype, designation, projectdescription, projectvalue, permitfee, squarefootage, or parishname (re-asserted by the pipeline's collapse step on the production pull).
dedupe_rule.rule: source_record_id = permitid. Collapse happens in the pipeline (registry collapse_events) before normalization; the in-batch duplicate gate and the DB upsert key remain as guards.

field_map.application_date: creationdate (the permit record's creation date; measured never after issueddate in the window)
field_map.category: designation — the source's own Residential / Commercial designation: Residential 5,088 permits, Commercial 2,290; 1,104 permits state no designation and carry NULL (never inferred)
field_map.contractor_rule: contractorname ONLY — the permit's published contractor of record, carried verbatim as the source prints it (some values append the contractor's contact person after a dash — the source's own format for its contractor field, carried as published, the Philadelphia treatment). 'N/A' (3,645 window rows) names no contractor and is carried as NULL. ownername and applicantname are person-name fields and contractoraddress is a contact field: all three are excluded from the pull's column list entirely and never requested from the API.
field_map.locality: city1 (a free-text mailing-city field: Baton Rouge in many spellings plus Zachary, Baker, Greenwell Springs, Pride, Slaughter, Jackson, Clinton; obvious Baton Rouge variants and unusable values normalize to Baton Rouge, the issuing jurisdiction's seat — display only, never a coverage scope)
field_map.permit_type_source: permittype (the type names the permit family directly; its (R)/(C) suffix restates the designation)
field_map.project_description: projectdescription (blank on 469 window permits — carried as NULL, never invented)
field_map.source_record_id: permitid (one published permit = one permit id; its per-address rows collapse — see dedupe_rule)
field_map.status_source: the dataset publishes NO status field; it is an issued-permits register, so status is 'issued' by the dataset's own definition and status_source stays NULL
field_map.valuation: projectvalue — the permit's stated project value, counted ONCE per permit (sibling rows restate it verbatim; measured zero disagreements). Validated 2026-10-18 (see audit): published on 100% of window permits; 63.6% of permits state more than $1 (the $0 majority sits in occupancy permits, which authorize a use rather than construction); no placeholder or sibling-stamp pathology (no value above $5M repeats at a different address; repeated large totals are round applicant budgets); two disclosed as-reported shapes — one multifamily project's $44,688,000 stated on each of its three building permits at the same address, and the $180,000,000 largest permit being a land-clearing permit carrying its whole project's value. The DB window sum must reproduce the independently computed $955,314,596.87. Values are applicants' stated figures, printed as reported (SOP rule 2).
